sources.note: Nothing. Syntax/discourse paper; only phonology content is Appendix A (9-10 vowel ATR chart, p.52) and one open question on p.51 ('does tone play a part in marking the beginning of the subordinate clause'). No mention of stress or accent anywhere (grep of full text).

sources.citation: Blench, Roger. 2020. The phonology and noun morphology of yi Kitule, an Adamawa language of East-Central Nigeria. Language in Africa 1(3): 155-180. (sister language Tula, checked for comparative remarks on Dadiya)
sources.note: Describes Tula (three level tones plus glides); full-text grep finds no mention of Dadiya prosody and no use of 'stress'/'accent'. Not a Dadiya source; not saved in the dadi1249 folder.

sources.citation: Anderson, Gregory D. S. 2016. STAMP morphs in the Macro-Sudan Belt. In Payne, Pacchiarotti & Bosire (eds.), Diversity in African languages: Selected papers from the 46th ACAL, 513-539. Berlin: Language Science Press.
sources.note: Second-hand typological survey; cites tone-marked Dadiya STAMP-morph/verb examples from Jungraithmayr 1968/69: 196-197 (ń já 'you have eaten', mə̀n nò-lɛ 'I am drinking'), confirming lexical/grammatical tone transcription in the primary source; nothing on stress.
